# Results — Study 722 (Logo-Rebrand)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — a corporate
**rebrand / logo change** is a **signal**, either of **renewal** (buy the fresh start) or of a
**floundering firm** (sell the vanity) — tested as a small **event study** over a hardcoded,
transparent table of ~26 real rebrands 2010–2025 (name changes, identity refreshes, logo-only
redesigns). Around each reveal we measure the abnormal (excess-of-SPY) return on a short
**announce** leg `[+1…+5d]` and a longer **drift** leg `[+6…+126d]` (~6 months), with a 1-day
entry lag. Offline & deterministic for the synthetic control; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + ~26 rebrand tickers (public, no key) |
| Window | 2008-01-02 → 2026-06-30 (cached); event windows fall within it |
| As-of / fingerprint | **2026-06-30**, `fp=c12adbfe3fd2` (4652 rows) |
| Rebrand table | **26** documented rebrands; **8** famous ones DELISTED / went private (named) |
| Events priced | **22** of 26 (rest delisted, listed after the announce, or window overran) |
| Announce / drift legs | abnormal excess-of-SPY return over `[+1…+5d]` (announce) and `[+6…+126d]` (drift) |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; large-cap one-way 10 bps × 2 crossings on the buy-and-hold book |

> **Survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The worst-outcome rebrands — **Twitter →
> X** (taken private 2023), **Weight Watchers → WW** (rename 2018, **Chapter 11 in 2025**),
> **Overstock → Bed Bath & Beyond** (bankrupt brand), **ViacomCBS → Paramount** (acquired 2025)
> — **left the tape** and leave **no** clean yfinance series. In fact, two of our four unpriced
> events (WW, Paramount) are *themselves* survivorship: the rebranded firm floundered or merged
> off the tape. The priced sample is therefore the set of rebrands that *survived*, biased
> **toward** names that did not collapse and **against** the believers' floundering thesis. A
> survivor-only drift that is *not negative* is thus a **conservative** refutation of "it's a
> floundering firm's tell."

## The signal — abnormal returns on each leg vs zero

1-day entry lag. The Welch *t* tests each leg's cross-sectional mean against zero; the placebo
*p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size non-event windows (same tickers) whose mean
abnormal return matches/beats the rebrand set in magnitude.

| leg | n | mean abnormal | win-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **announce** `[+1…+5d]`  | 22 | **+2.44%** | 64% | **+1.96** | 0.022 |
| **drift** `[+6…+126d]`   | 22 | **−4.61%** | 45% | **−1.05** | 0.333 |

Read it carefully. The **drift** — the leg that carries the renewal/floundering claim — is
**−4.6%** at **t = −1.05** (placebo *p* = 0.33): statistically zero, and slightly negative only
on a tape already biased *up* by survivorship. Neither camp lands: renewal wants the drift
clearly **positive**, the skeptic wants it clearly **negative**, and it is neither. The
**announce** leg is a **+2.4%** first-week pop that looks alive (placebo *p* = 0.022) but
**fails the t ≥ 2 bar** and, as the fragility table shows, is two confounded outliers deep.

## By rebrand kind — the "signal" is reverse causation

| kind | n | mean announce | mean drift |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| name change | 8 | +3.56% | **−16.40%** |
| identity / structure | 5 | +0.64% | −9.06% |
| logo-only refresh | 9 | +2.45% | **+8.34%** |

The drift splits by *who rebrands how*: **name changes drift down**, **logo-only refreshes
drift up** — opposite signs. That is not a rebrand effect; it is **reverse causation**. Firms
in trouble tend to change their *name* (Weight Watchers → WW, ViacomCBS → Paramount); healthy
giants merely *restyle* (Pepsi, J&J, Mastercard, Walmart). The "signal" is the firm's
pre-existing health, read backwards — not a forward-looking edge.

## Fragility — the week-one pop is two headlines deep

Drop the largest-|announce| events one at a time and re-test the pop:

| dropped | n | mean announce | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 (none) | 22 | +2.44% | **+1.96** |
| 1 | 21 | +1.71% | +1.62 |
| 2 | 20 | +1.02% | +1.21 |
| 3 | 19 | +0.68% | +0.84 |

The two names doing the heavy lifting — **GM** (+17.8%, mid-EV-re-rating) and **BlackBerry**
(+15.6%, whose pop was really the BB10 phone-launch week) — moved on *product/strategy* news,
not a logo. Strip those confounds and the "rebrand pop" is indistinguishable from zero. This is
why the announce leg stamps `WEAK`, not `REAL`.

## The believers' trade loses money — before costs even bite

The renewal camp's trade is: **buy the reveal (day+1), hold the drift window, exit.** Per event
that is `announce + drift`.

| | per-event P&L |
|---|--:|
| gross hold (announce + drift) | **−2.17%** |
| net @ 10 bps/leg × 2 crossings | **−2.37%** |

Because the six-month drift is soft-negative, buy-and-hold **loses** — **−2.2% gross**, **−2.4%
net**. The skeptic's fade trade is just the sign-flip, and its "profit" comes entirely from the
survivorship-inflated few percent, well inside the noise. There is nothing to harvest.

## Robustness — the result is flat in the window choice

| announce / drift days | n | announce mean | announce *t* | drift mean | drift *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 / 60   | 22 | +1.74% | +1.78 | −1.70% | −0.51 |
| **5 / 120** | 22 | +2.44% | +1.96 | −4.61% | −1.05 |
| 5 / 252  | 22 | +2.44% | +1.96 | −9.18% | −1.38 |
| 10 / 120 | 22 | +2.27% | +1.29 | −4.85% | −1.32 |
| 1 / 120  | 22 | +0.24% | +0.34 | −1.82% | −0.38 |

No window makes the announce pop clear *t* = 2 (a 1-day window drops it to *t* = 0.34), and the
drift is insignificant and soft-negative at every horizon. The verdict does not hinge on the
exact window.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and ~26 events are weak

On deterministic event windows where we *plant* a known renewal drift of size `edge`:

| planted edge | n | announce mean | announce *t* | drift mean | drift *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 26 | −0.32% | −0.31 | −0.52% | −0.10 |
| **+0.30** (large renewal) | 26 | −0.32% | −0.31 | +34.28% | +5.05 |

With **no** planted edge the drift leg stays flat (it cannot manufacture significance from ~26
noisy events). Only a **large** planted +30% renewal drift lights the drift leg up (*t* = +5.1).
The control proves the measurement engine is unbiased **and** that a couple-dozen events can
only detect an implausibly large effect — exactly why a survivor table of ~22 rebrands cannot
certify the legend.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The renewal/floundering claim lives in the **drift**, which is **−4.6%** at
  **t = −1.05** (placebo *p* = 0.33) — a `NONE`, and slightly negative only on a survivorship-
  inflated tape. The one flicker of life, a **+2.4%** week-one pop, is significant *raw*
  (placebo *p* = 0.022) but **fails t ≥ 2** and **collapses to t = 1.21** when two news-confounded
  outliers (GM, BlackBerry) drop — a fragile `WEAK`, not `REAL`. Survivorship is named on this
  axis: the worst-outcome rebrands delisted / went private, biasing the drift *up*.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Buy-the-rebrand-and-hold is **−2.2% gross** / **−2.4% net** per
  event; the soft-negative drift eats the little pop, and the pop leg itself isn't investable
  (sub-*t*=2, outlier-built). There is no edge to harvest, at any size.
- **Renewal or red-flag? — COIN FLIP.** The drift cannot separate the two: name-changes drift
  **−16%**, logo refreshes **+8%** — the firm's *prior* health leaking through backwards, not a
  forward signal. A rebrand is a coin flip wearing a new logo.
